en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Section on the Refutation of Difficulties (Meṇḍakapañha Paṇāmitavagga)
6. The Question on the Great Fruit of Almsfood “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Elders who compiled the Dhamma:
‘Having eaten the meal of Cunda, [the Blessed One fell ill].’”
"I have heard, O smith,
that a wise man has been struck by a severe, terminal illness."
Furthermore, it was said by the Blessed One:
“Ānanda, these two alms-offerings are equal in fruit, equal in result, and far more fruitful and beneficial than other alms-offerings.
Which two?”

"The alms-food which the Tathāgata consumed and then awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and the alms-food which the Tathāgata consumed and then attained final Nibbāna in the element of Nibbāna without residue—these two alms-meals have equal fruits and equal results;
they are far more productive of great fruit and greater benefit than any other alms-meals.
"Venerable Nāgasena, if a severe illness arose in the Blessed One after he had eaten Cunda’s meal..."
And since intense, deathly painful sensations have arisen, then that statement— “These two alms-offerings,
Ānanda, are equal in fruit, equal in result, and far more fruitful and beneficial than other alms-offerings”— is false.
If these two alms-meals are equal in fruit and equal in result, being far more fruitful and more beneficial than other alms-meals,
then that statement— that after the Blessed One had eaten Cunda’s meal,
a severe illness arose in him and agonizing, deathly pains set in— is false.

“Venerable Nāgasena, was that alms-food productive of great fruit because it contained poison, because it caused the arising of disease, because it destroyed life, or because it took away the Blessed One’s life?
Tell me the reason for this in order to refute the arguments of opponents; for in this matter people are confused, thinking that because he ate too much out of greed, dysentery arose.
This too is a double-pronged question that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.”
“Great King, this was indeed spoken by the Elders who compiled the Dhamma:
‘Having eaten the meal of Cunda the smith—
so have I heard— ’”
“The wise man is touched by affliction,
severe and leading to death.
And it was said by the Blessed One:
“Ānanda, these two alms-meals are equal in fruit and equal in result, and they are far more fruitful and far more beneficial than other alms-meals.
Which two?
The alms-meal which, having consumed, the Tathāgata awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment; and [the second is]...”
"And that almsfood which the Tathāgata, having consumed, attains final nibbāna in the element of nibbāna without residue—
these two almsfoods have equal fruits and equal results; they are far more fruitful and far more beneficial than other almsfoods."
Furthermore, that alms-food was of many virtues and manifold benefits.
O Great King, the deities, joyful and with serene minds, thinking, "This is the final alms-food of the Blessed One," infused divine essence into the *sūkaramaddava*.
And that was perfectly cooked, light to digest, delightful, full of flavor, and beneficial for the digestive heat of the stomach.

"No, Great King, no disease whatsoever arose in the Blessed One on that account. Rather, Great King, because the Blessed One’s body was naturally frail and the constituent of his life-force was exhausted, the disease that had arisen increased all the more.
Just as a fire, Great King, which is burning by its own nature, blazes up even more when other fuel is added;
even so, Great King, because the Blessed One’s body was naturally frail and the constituent of his life-force was exhausted, the disease that had arisen increased all the more."
Or again, Great King, just as a stream that flows naturally becomes a much greater flood carrying away water when a great rain-cloud has poured down;
even so, Great King, while the Blessed One’s body was naturally weak and the constituent forces of his life-span were exhausted, the disease that arose increased all the more.
Or again, Great King, just as a stomach whose humors are already naturally saturated would expand further when something else is swallowed; [even so did the disease increase].
“In the same way, Great King, while the Blessed One’s body was naturally weak and the constituent of his lifespan had been exhausted, the illness that arose increased all the more.
There is no fault, Great King, in that alms-food; nor is it possible to impute any fault to it.
“Venerable Nāgasena, for what reason were those two alms-meals equal in fruit and equal in result, and why were they far more fruitful and of greater benefit than other alms-meals?”

“By way of the attainment of reflection upon the Dhamma, O Great King, those two alms-meals have equal fruit and equal result, and they are far more fruitful and more beneficial than other alms-meals.
“But, venerable Nāgasena, by way of reflection upon which things do those two alms-meals have equal fruit and equal result, and are far more fruitful and more beneficial than other alms-meals?”
“Great king, by virtue of entering those two alms-offerings in both forward and reverse order through the nine successive meditative attainments,
they are equal in fruit and equal in result, and are far more productive of great fruit and great benefit than other alms-offerings.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, was it on two days alone that the Tathāgata attained the nine successive meditative attainments in both forward and reverse order?
“Yes, Great King.
“It is wonderful, Venerable Nāgasena! It is marvelous, Venerable Nāgasena!”
Even that peerless, supreme gift which exists in this Buddha-field is not equal to these two alms-offerings.
It is wonderful, venerable Nāgasena; it is marvelous, venerable Nāgasena!

How great indeed are the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling, in that by means of these nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling, a gift becomes more fruitful and more beneficial.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.
This is the sixth discourse on the great fruitfulness of almsfood.
